children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a weak start on November 20, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is trading lower at 25,340 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol
Indian benchmark indices staged a strong recovery on November 19, with the Nifty climbing above 25,500 mark, as buying interest was seen across most sectors, barring information technology stocks.
At close, the Sensex was up 989.94 points or 1.21 percent at 83,021.75, and the Nifty was up 286.35 points or 1.14 percent at 25,514.30.

On the sectoral front, the Nifty Auto index led the rally, surging 4.4 percent, followed by Consumer Durables, which gained 3.2 percent. Nifty PSU Bank advanced 2.2 percent, while FMCG rose 1.9 percent. Nifty Private Bank and Nifty Bank added 1.4 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively. However, the Nifty IT index declined 1.1 percent.
The broader markets also ended higher, with the Nifty Midcap index gaining 0.9 percent and the Nifty Smallcap index advancing 0.7 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Down)
GIFT Nifty was trading lower at around 25,340 in early trade, indicating a weak opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Down)

Asian stocks sold off as pessimism over the artificial-intelligence trade hammered technology shares, with global equities set for their longest losing streak in three years. Anthropic PBC fell in after-hours trading.

MSCI Inc.’s Asia Pacific equities index fell 1.7% — extending its decline to a seventh straight session — and poised for its lowest close since April. That pushed the MSCI All Country World Index — a key barometer of global stocks - on course for its longest losing streak since September 2023.
US Equities (Slip)
US stocks slumped on Thursday, after Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed ​to revitalize faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its share price ebbed.
Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 a share and quickly ‌rose as high as $115 a share, or 38.6% above the offer price, but pared those gains to 17.1% by the end of the session.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, the S&P 500 lost 147.80 points, or 2.02%, to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 550.68 points, or 2.25%, to 23,879.20.
Dollar Index (Down)

The dollar is headed for a fourth straight weekly gain as demand tied to the Anthropic PBC IPO further lifts the currency that has been supported by expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes and elevated US
Treasury yields.
US Bond Yield (Down)
The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to a one-week low of 5.016% in early Asia trade and is down 10 basis points on the week.
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasury bonds shed 2 basis points each at 5.02% and 4.74%, respectively.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with most regional currencies registering losses. The Philippine peso was the worst performer, declining 0.31%, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which fell 0.27%. The Chinese renminbi weakened 0.18%, while the South Korean won and Indonesian rupiah slipped 0.15% and 0.12%, respectively. The Malaysian ringgit edged down 0.03%.
On the positive side, the Japanese yen gained 0.19%, emerging as the best-performing currency in the region, while the Thai baht and Singapore dollar edged higher by 0.06% and 0.04%, respectively.
Crude (Up)
Oil edged higher after a volatile session on Thursday, with futures on track for a third weekly decline as traders weigh the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran against ample supply.

Brent traded above $92 a barrel after swinging in a range of more than $2 in the previous session, and is down almost 4% this week. The most-active contract for West Texas Intermediate traded near $83.
Gold (Down)

Gold fell and was heading for the biggest weekly decline since March, as a hawkish Federal Reserve signaled more interest-rate hikes and a rout in AI stocks pushed investors to sell the metal to cover losses.

Bullion dropped as much as 1.1% on Friday to below $3,590 an ounce, and was on track to lose about 7% in a week that’s seen the metal slide to the lowest since September 2025. Silver has fallen around 13% in the same period.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak to the eighth consecutive session on November 19, purchasing equities worth Rs 7,411 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued their selling for the second straight session, offloading equities worth Rs 1,356 crore.
